newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam PM says no favours for state sector.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam PM says no favours for state sector.

text.p: Vietnam's Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has said Hanoi will adopt a level playing field approach towards public and private businesses, despite its determination to promote the state sector.
In an interview with Thursday's Tuoi Tre newspaper, Kiet denied suggestions policy was contradictory and said all business, whether state-owned, private, or foreign would be treated equally.

"I do not think there is any contradiction. The state sector is being built as the core," he said. "(But) we should make all efforts to reach equality, then conditions will be created to encourage other economic sectors to develop."
Kiet's comments follow the unveiling in June of a five-year policy plan which enshrined directives aimed at establishing a leading role for state-owned enterprise in the economy.

At present the sector and cooperatives account for around 40 percent of gross domestic product aPLGDP against 60 percent for private businesses, which have multiplied under reform and open-door policies introduced in the late 1980s.
But Kiet stressed the five-year directives were not aimed at creating more favourable conditions for the state sector than for others.
"It (government policy) means to ensure equality for all economic sectors, including state-owned, non-state as well as the foreign sector," he said.
Vietnam's state sector is a remnant of the Soviet-style economic system which preceded market-led reforms.
Economists say the sector suffers gross inefficiency, a shortage of capital for modernising and an absence of technology and marketing expertise.
